utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay, I think everyone's here. Ingrid, you're muted - no, you're on.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, I was just finishing a thing with Zofia about the dock schedule. Morning.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Morning. Is this the packaging thing or the other thing?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Packaging. Northern warehouse.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Oh good, I have opinions about that.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: You always have opinions.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That's the point of me being here.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Right. So, um, where we are is, the boxes keep running out up there and nobody likes how it's been going.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Last month we had two mornings where the packers were waiting on cartons. I logged both.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Was that the Tuesday when the van broke down? Because I heard Bilal say the van broke down and that was why-

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Different van. That was the inbound pallets.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Oh. Okay. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: So what's the fix. Lena, you had something?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Yeah, so, I've been thinking about it as, like, stop ordering when we panic and just get it on a rhythm. A weekly standing order with Calder, for all the corrugated and the void-fill, northern only.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Everything? Both?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Both, yeah. One order, one day, done.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: What's the weekly volume you're picturing? Because the void-fill moves differently from the cartons.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Um, roughly what we use now, I'd say. I haven't got the sheet in front of me.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It's about, hmm, fourteen hundred cartons a week on average, but it swings.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: See, that swing is my worry. A fixed order on a swinging number.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Right, but that's sort of the thing. Calder gets it to us inside forty-eight hours, so we don't need to hold a big cushion.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: We could hold around five days of stock instead of what, three weeks? And that frees up something like a hundred and forty pallet positions.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: At eleven pounds a position a month, that's-

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Yeah, don't make me do it, it's like fifteen hundred a month, give or take.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Fifteen forty, if it's exactly one-forty.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: There you go.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: That's a lot of floor space. When I was at the old site we had a whole aisle just full of mailer bags nobody used and-

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Ingrid.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Right. Yes. Sorry. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Okay, devil's advocate. Forty-eight hours is what they say. What do they actually do?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I have the last six months from the portal. Mostly inside two days. Twice it was three.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Twice it was three. So that's the two mornings.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: No, the two mornings were before we used the portal. Different cause.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Mm. Okay.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And if it slips we just have five days of cover, which is still-

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Five days isn't a lot when it slips by three.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It's two days of margin, though.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: A bit thin.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Can I just say, did anyone else get the email about the badge readers? Because mine stopped working on the east door yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Not now, Ingrid.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Okay. Later.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Mine worked fine.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: It's probably just mine.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Back to it. What happens at peak? The July stuff.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Well, that's, um, I'd have to ask Oksana what Calder said about peak.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Oksana told me they hold buffer for standing customers. Standing orders get priority over the ad hoc ones.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That's a point for it, I guess.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I'm not agreeing. I'm acknowledging.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: And the price? Is it the same per unit on a standing order?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Same or slightly better, I think. I'd want to double check with Bao.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Bao quoted me two percent under list for committed volume. That was in April.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: See, that's even better then.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Unless the committed volume bites us.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: There's no minimum on the quote, there's a, um, a band. Plus or minus twenty percent we can change without a fee.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Plus or minus twenty. Okay, that's more reasonable than I thought.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Is that written down anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It's in the quote. I can forward it.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Yes please.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: So it's basically, it's just a way of not having to think about it every week.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Which is what people say right before they stop checking.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: We'd still check. The stock count is on Mondays anyway.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Fine. But someone owns the Monday check.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I can. For now.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: I could do it too, I'm up there on Mondays anyway for-

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It's fine, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: What about the existing orders? Joao had a couple of open ones, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Two open with the old supplier, both delivering by the twentieth. They'd just run off.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: So no overlap problem.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: A bit of overlap, we'd have a lot of boxes for a week or so.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That's fine, nobody ever complained about too many boxes.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Actually, there was a time at the other site where we had so many-

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Ingrid.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Anyone else got a concern? Before I-

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: One more. If Calder has a bad month, who do we call?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Their account person. Elif's got the number.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I do. And the old supplier is still on the system if we need a one-off.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: So we're not locked out of the other route.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: No. It's just not the default.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Okay. That's a decent answer. I'll stop.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: That's it?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: For now.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay. Then the northern warehouse gets its corrugated and void-fill from the weekly Calder standing order. That's how we're doing it.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Brilliant.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Do you want me to tell Bao, or you?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: You do it. Cc me.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Will do. I'll ask about the first delivery date as well.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Can we make it a Thursday? Thursdays are quiet on the dock.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'll ask. Might depend on their routes.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Thursday's good. Thursdays Ines is off, so there's less people in the way.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I'd still like the Monday check in writing somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'll put a line in the weekly sheet.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Okay, so, the badge thing. I think it might actually be the whole east door and not just mine.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Raise it with facilities.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Facilities is Zofia's thing, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It's Bilal now.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Since when?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Since the reorg. March, I think.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: April.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: April, whatever.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Okay, I'll ping Bilal then.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: No, I think that's us.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I've got a call at half past.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Then that's it. Thanks, all.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Bye!

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Right, we're all here. Before anything, did the Thursday slot go through with Calder?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes, first drop was last Thursday, came in at ten past nine. Fine.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Oh good. Did the cartons look okay? I heard someone say the corners were crushed.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: That was one pallet. Bottom layer, I took photos.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Was that the pallet that sat outside because the dock was busy? Because Zofia said something about the dock being full and then-

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Let him talk, Ingrid, he's got something.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Yeah. Um. I got a call from Oksana yesterday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: About the Calder thing?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: About Calder, yes. They're shutting the northern depot. Six weeks from now.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Shutting it. Like fully?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Fully. So what we get comes up from the Midlands instead, and that's a five-day lead, not two. Plus they add four hundred and fifty a drop.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Four fifty per delivery? Not per pallet?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Per drop. It's in the email, I'll forward it.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Huh. That's not great.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Five days. So the whole forty-eight hours business-

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: That's the bit. The stock level we picked was built on getting a top-up inside two days. That's gone.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: So I'd like to look at it again. Properly. Not just tweak the number.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Fair. Five days of cover with a five day lead means we're basically ordering on the day we run out.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Right, so the whole idea sort of falls over.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Does it though? You could just hold more.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: More than five days, sure, but then you're back to the floor space we wanted to give up.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Which is a cost, not a disaster.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Can I ask what the weekly drops cost now? Before the closure I mean.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Nothing extra. It was in the unit price.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Okay, so it's all new money then.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is the old supplier still an option? The one we used before?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: They're on the system. Their lead time was never great though, and I don't have a current quote.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: What about the other one, the paper mill? Fenmoor. Didn't Bao get a figure from them?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Bao did, back in the spring. I'd have to find it.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: I've got it, actually. It was in that thread with Joao.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: So, um, Fenmoor came in about eight percent under on the tonne. And that's for the month's worth in one go.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: One go. So that's the monthly bulk thing.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Right. And the catch is you need somewhere to put it. A buffer of about three weeks sitting at the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Which is a lot of boxes.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: It's roughly ninety pallet positions. At what we pay per position that's about a thousand a month, give or take.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Ninety times eleven. Nine-ninety. Yes, call it a thousand.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: And the Calder way, with the surcharge, you'd have four drops a month. Four fifty each. That's, um, eighteen hundred.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: So the storage is cheaper than the surcharges.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: By a fair margin, and you also get the lower price on the paper. And three weeks of cover means a late truck doesn't hurt.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Devil's advocate. Three weeks of stock is exactly what we said we didn't want.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: We said we didn't want it when it was free to avoid. Now it isn't.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Hm. Okay. That's not a bad answer.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And the space is there? In the northern building?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It's there. Ninety positions is the same as what we freed up, nearly.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: So it's like going back to before, but cheaper.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Roughly, yes. The paper price is the difference.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: And no minimum from Fenmoor?

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Um, I don't remember. I think there's a minimum drop size.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'll check the quote. It's a monthly volume anyway, so we'd be over it.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay. Then the northern warehouse moves to the monthly Fenmoor bulk order, with the three-week buffer.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay, great.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Do I tell Bao, or Oksana, about Calder stopping the weekly?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Tell Oksana. She should hear it from us before the depot thing is official.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Will do. I'll keep the Monday count going.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Please do. More stock, more to lose track of.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It's in the sheet already.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is there anything else on this, or are we done? I've got a thing at eleven.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: One other item. Ingrid, the dock.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Right, yes. The carriers. Okay so, what if we give them two-hour appointment windows, rather than the whole day?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Instead of all-day, you mean.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Yeah. Instead of the whole day.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is that a big change for them?

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Not really, most of the big ones already do it at other sites.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Why now?

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Because of the yard. The trucks are sitting there about ninety-five minutes on average, I pulled it from the gate log.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Ninety-five. That's a lot.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: And then most afternoons the dock itself is empty for, I want to say three hours. Nothing coming in at all.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: So everyone turns up in the morning because they can.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Exactly that. And Zofia says it's the same mess every day.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: That does sound daft when you say it like that.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Any downside? Drivers hate being held to a time.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: They hate sitting on our yard more.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Fair.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay. Two-hour windows for carriers, starting with the next booking round.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: I'll draft the note to them. And Ines will need to know for the gate.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Copy Bilal as well.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Will do. Sorry, was Bilal facilities or is that still Zofia?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Bilal.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Right. That's us, thanks.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay, we're all here. Um, let's start with the Fenmoor side, since that's the one with dates on it.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I checked the quote like I said. The minimum drop is eight pallets, so the monthly volume clears it easily.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Eight. And we'd be doing, what, forty-odd a month?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Closer to fifty. It's in the sheet.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Good. So that's, that's not an issue then.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: No. The thing I don't have is a first delivery date.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Did you ask?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I asked Bao to ask them. He said he'd come back this week.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: When does Calder actually stop up north? I had six weeks from the call.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: End of July, if I count it from the email. I'd have to look at the exact day.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: So it's sort of a month and a bit from now.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: About that. Which matters, because the first Fenmoor load has to land before then, not after.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Or you have a gap with nothing coming.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes. That's the gap I don't love.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Could the last Calder drops just cover it?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: They could, if the weekly ones keep running until the depot shuts. I'd want that in writing.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Mm. Ask Oksana.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'll put it in the same email.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: And the buffer, does it have to be full on day one? Or does it build up?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It builds. The first month's load is the buffer, more or less. Then each month tops it up.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: So the first few weeks you're thin.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Thin, yes, but with Calder still running that's covered.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Right. Right, that makes sense.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Can I ask about the pallet positions? Where are the ninety actually going? Is it the back bay?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Aisles fourteen to seventeen, the ones we cleared in the spring.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Oh, those. Those were full of the returns stuff before, weren't they. Did anyone ever-

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: They're clear.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Okay. Good.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Who checks that? Because "clear" in my experience means "clear apart from three pallets".

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I walked it on Tuesday. Two empty racks have a bent beam, though.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is that bad?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It's a safety thing, they can't be loaded until it's fixed. So maybe eighty-five usable. Maybe less.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Eighty-five. Ha. So not quite ninety.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Close enough for the first month. I've asked maintenance for a date.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Who's maintenance, Bilal?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Bilal's got the request, yes.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is that going to eat into the budget?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It's an existing line. I don't think it's anything we have to find.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay. I just wanted to be sure that wasn't coming out of us.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: What about the Monday count? Is it still just the one sheet?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: One sheet. I'm adding a column for weeks of cover, so you can see it drop.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Weeks, not days.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Weeks now, yes. Days looks silly at that level.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Fine. Someone other than you should be able to read it though.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It's got a note at the top.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Anything else on this one? Otherwise I'd like to get the others.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Just that I'll tell the others upstairs once there's a date.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Please. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'll send it round once Bao replies.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Good. Next. The carrier note. Ingrid, where's that?

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Drafted. It's basically one page. Two-hour windows, from the first booking round in July.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Did Ines see it?

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: She did, she's fine with the gate part. She did ask whether the windows are fixed or if carriers can swap.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Can they?

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Um, I put that they can swap with a day's notice, but I'm not sure that's right.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: A day's notice will become no notice in a week.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Leave it as is for now. See how it goes.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Okay. And Bilal asked to be copied, so I did.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Did anyone see the thing from Zofia about the fire door signage?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Is that the one with the new stickers?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Yes, that. She wants the stickers done by the end of the month.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: It's a sticker.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It's sixty doors.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Oh. Okay, that's a different sticker.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I can do the northern ones. Southern's someone else.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Great, thanks.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Anyone else got something? Priya?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Quarterly review. I need a number from each of you for the supplier scorecard by Friday.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: What number?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: On-time delivery and any complaints. Same as last quarter.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Oh. Is that the one with the colours?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Red, amber, green. Yes.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Right. I don't have mine.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Mine's done. I'll send it after this.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: I think mine's mostly done. There was a Calder complaint that I wasn't sure about.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: The crushed corners one? Or was that Elif's photos.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: That was mine. One pallet.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Then I haven't got any. Great.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Please check, though.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Yes, will do.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay. Um. One more thing, the offsite.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: The one in September?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Yes. Finance wants numbers by the end of next week.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: How many are we?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: The five of us. Maybe Bao as well.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Bao isn't in our team.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: He's on the supplier side. I'll check if it's allowed.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is the train covered?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Standard class, yes.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Can we do a hotel that isn't next to the ring road this time?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: I'll ask. No promises.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Thanks. That was a bad week.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It was really loud.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I slept fine.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: You sleep fine anywhere.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Right. Back to the warehouse for a second. Elif, the Calder weekly orders still open, how many?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Two. This Thursday and next Thursday, both already placed.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: And after that, nothing's booked?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Not yet. I'd rather wait for Oksana's reply before I place any more.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: What if she's slow?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Then I'll chase. I don't want to put a third one in blind.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And if Fenmoor can't hit the date, we've got a hole.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: That's the hole I mentioned. I'm saying it out loud so it's said.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Noted. I'll keep it on the risk list.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is there a risk list?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: There is now.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Ha. Okay.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: I've got to jump, I've got finance at half past. Elif, you'll keep everyone posted?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes, tomorrow once I've heard from Bao.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Thanks, all.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Bye!

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, is everyone here? Lena, you're on mute, I can see your mouth moving.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, I was - yeah. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yes. Good. So Chidi sent apologies, he's stuck at the depot all morning.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Is that the one with the broken dock door again? Because Sione told me last week that-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Diego, hold that thought, we've got a packed hour.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Right, right. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: First thing, the quarterly stock count. Arjun, where are we?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Done for two sites. Third one Friday.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Friday this week or next?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: This week.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Fine. Any blockers?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: No. Need the scanners back from Bao's team.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I'll ping Bao. Put it in the thread so I don't forget.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Can I ask about the audit thing, is that still on the, um, the fourteenth?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I think it moved. Valeria said something about the week after, but don't quote me.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay, I'll check with her. I just need to know for the leave calendar.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yeah, do that.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: So, uh, before we run out of time, can we do the parcel thing? The south-east one?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Sure. Remind me where we left it, I've lost the thread.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Well, we've been, you know, sort of going round on it for weeks. Our current setup there is, it's a bit of a patchwork.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: It really is. We've got like three different local couriers, and one of them only does Tuesdays and-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Right, which is part of why I - so, what I'd put forward is, um, just moving the whole south-east over to Parcelwise. All of it. Twelve months, four pounds ten a parcel.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: All of it? Not just the busy postcodes?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: All of it, yeah. Simpler.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Why simpler?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: One carrier, one contract, one set of, uh, labels. I mean, that's the big picture.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And the price, is it-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Hang on, let me get to the numbers, I have them somewhere. Okay. What we pay now averages out around four eighty-five.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: And the region does something like eighteen thousand parcels in a quarter. Give or take.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: So you take that gap on each one, times the volume, and it comes to roughly thirteen and a half thousand a quarter back in our pocket.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Thirteen and a half. Is that a real number or a back-of-envelope one?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Back of envelope, but it's close. Pretty sure it's close.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: It's close. Seventy-five pence times eighteen.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. Let me push on it though. Four ten is a quoted rate. What does it look like after surcharges?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I, um, I don't have the surcharge sheet in front of me.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: There's a fuel one, isn't there? Because last time with the other carrier we-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Lena, let him answer.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: The quote says fuel is included. I think. I'd have to check the wording.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So the answer is you think.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I'm fairly sure, yes.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: This reminds me, when I was at my last place we had a carrier quote us a flat rate and then it turned out the flat rate stopped at two kilos. Every parcel over that was a different price. Nobody read page four.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Average parcel weight here is under two.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Is it? Okay. Good. Because that was a nightmare, we had a whole spreadsheet, the finance lead went grey.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Diego, the tangent. Brief.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Brief. Yes. Sorry. Anyway, it's fine then.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: What about the contract being twelve months? What if they're bad?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Well, there's a, uh, an exit clause. Maybe. Alejandra mentioned one.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I can confirm it. I will confirm it.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Service levels?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: They're national, so, you know, they've got the network. Delivery times are in the pack.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: What are they?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Next day for most postcodes. I'd have to look at the, the exact -

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Fine. Look later.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Can I ask something totally different for a sec? Who's covering the returns desk on the twenty-ninth? Because I'm out.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Dalia had it, I think. I'll check. Let's not bury the parcel thing.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, it just popped into my head.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: And did anyone see the email about the new label printers? Apparently there's a new model, and the old ones don't take the roll size.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Not relevant.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: It's kind of relevant if we change carriers though.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Is it?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Well - the label format. If it's Parcelwise labels it might be a different stock.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Oh. Yeah, I hadn't thought about that. I'd guess it's the same.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Guess.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: It's a standard thermal thing, I think. Everyone uses the same roll.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. Park it. Somebody check with Bao on that, he did the printer order.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I can do that.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Good. So, devil's advocate for a second. We're sitting on three local couriers who know the lanes. We move everything to one national carrier and if their depot has a bad week, the whole region goes down together.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: That's true. It's a concentration thing.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Locals aren't reliable either.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Not saying they are. Saying we trade one risk for another.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: But the Tuesday one, the, the, the one that only does Tuesdays, honestly that's -

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: It's embarrassing, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Customers complain about it constantly.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Do they? How many complaints last quarter?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I don't have it. Quite a few. Maybe a dozen a month?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Dozen is right. I counted in July.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. So that's one thing in favour of changing.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: And the saving. The saving is still the main point, to me.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I know. I'm just making sure we're not signing something because the headline number is nice.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Sure, yeah, no, fair.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Number is nice though.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It is. It's a good number.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Can I just say, thirteen thousand a quarter, that's basically a person's, um, a chunk of someone's salary. That's not nothing.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Please don't turn it into headcount.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: No, no, just saying.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is anybody else worried that we'll get stuck with the twelve months if we sign now and then, like, a better quote shows up in the spring?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: That's the same question as before. Dmitri, exit clause, you'll confirm.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I'll confirm it today. I'll email Alejandra.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Fine. And I'm not hearing anyone with a competing proposal, right? Nobody has anything else on the table?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Not me.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: No, just the exit thing.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Then I'm happy. South-east parcels go to Parcelwise, twelve months at the rate Dmitri quoted, subject to the exit clause check.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Great. Thanks. I'll get the paperwork started.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Fine by me.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Dmitri, copy me on the email to Alejandra. Lena, check the audit date with Valeria. Diego, the label question for Bao.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: On it.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Will do. Sorry again for the mute thing.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It's fine. Okay, that's us, I've got another call.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, we're all here? Dmitri, you're frozen, or is that just your face.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Ha, no, I'm here. Sorry, the connection's a bit - yeah. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Loud and clear. Right, let's start with the returns desk because I said I'd check. Dalia has the twenty-ninth, Lena, you're fine.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Oh good, thanks, I was going to ask again, because I-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It's sorted. Moving on.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay, thanks.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Did the audit date ever get confirmed? Lena, you were going to ask Valeria.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Yes, so it's the week after, not the fourteenth. I think the twenty-first. Maybe the twenty-second.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Which?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Um, I'll look. It was in her email.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Put it in the thread.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Can I ask about the label stock first? Because Bao got back to me and it's, well, it's not what Dmitri said, I mean it kind of is-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Diego, short version.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Short version, the rolls are the same width, the printers are fine. Nothing to do.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Oh good. Told you it was a standard thing.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: You guessed.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Educated guess.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Diego. Now, we're about five weeks into the south-east thing, so I wanted to see how it's going. Anyone looked at it?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Honestly, from what I can see it's going fine. Volumes are flowing, labels are printing, the paperwork's done-

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is the exit clause thing -

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Yes, Alejandra confirmed it, I forwarded it. Sorry, I should have said at the time.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Fine. Arjun, you've been in the delivery data, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Yes. Pulled it Monday.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Not great.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Not great how?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Parcelwise is landing eighty-one percent on time. The regional couriers were at ninety-six over the same stretch last quarter. That's about six hundred and forty late parcels so far.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Sorry, eighty-one? Is that - which measure is that?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Delivered by the promised date. Same definition we always use.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Right. Okay. I mean, it's early days, they're still ramping up, you know?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Five weeks.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Sure, but new lanes always-

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Where are they late, though? Is it everywhere, or is it one depot, because last time with the other carrier it was just the one hub and-

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Mostly the coastal postcodes. Not only.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay, so that's - yeah.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Let me poke at that. If it's a ramp-up thing, then the number should be getting better week on week. Is it?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Slightly. Seventy-eight, then eighty-one, roughly.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Roughly. I can send the sheet.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: So it's trending up, that's the big picture. That's encouraging.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: It's not that encouraging, if you're one of the customers though. I mean-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Go on, Diego.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: No, because we've had the credits. Finance sent me the figure on Tuesday, I've been sitting on it. We've given back nineteen hundred pounds in customer credits just in these five weeks.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Nineteen hundred.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: About that, yes. And that's before the, um, the three enterprise accounts. Three of them have complained, properly, to their account managers. One of them copied somebody quite senior.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Which three?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: The ones you'd expect. I'd rather not list them on a call. But the saving everyone liked, it's thirteen thousand a quarter on paper, and I just don't think it holds up if we're handing back money and annoying the people who pay the most.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Well, the credits are a one-off, though, aren't they? Once the service settles-

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Are they? They're not a one-off if it's still at eighty-one.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And the credits are only the ones that asked. Most people just don't bother, they just quietly-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Lena, let Diego finish.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Sorry. Go on.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: That's basically it. It reminds me of, uh, when we had the pallet network at my old place, we kept getting told it was a teething problem, and it was, it was teething for about fourteen months.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Diego.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Right. Sorry. Teething. Done.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Fine point though.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, let me play the other side for a minute, because somebody should. Nineteen hundred over five weeks is, what, not even half the quarterly saving?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: It's - yes. Well under half.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So on cash alone we're still ahead.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: On cash.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: On cash. But I'm not sure what a complaint to an enterprise account costs us.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Exactly. That's the bit nobody's put a number on.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Can I just - sorry - the Tuesday courier, remember, we were getting complaints about that all the time? Are the complaints now more or fewer than when we had the locals?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Don't know. Haven't split them.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Because that matters, doesn't it, if it's the same people just complaining about a different thing-

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: It's not the same people. These are the big accounts, the ones on service agreements.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Oh, that's different, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I think we should maybe talk to Parcelwise first. Before we, you know, react. They might have a plan for it.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Have you spoken to them?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Not about this. Not yet. I've got a contact there, I'd just ring them.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Which contact?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: The, um, account person. Their name's on the contract. I'd have to look.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Look.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I will, I will. Yes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Let's say you do. What do you ask them?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: What they're doing about the coast. And whether they, I don't know, whether there's any, uh, service credit on their side.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: That's a good question actually. The contract might have something. Has anyone read the service level part?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I read the, the front. Mostly.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Nobody read page four.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Ha. Okay, that one's fair.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Right, okay. Is there a quick answer on the service level clause? Dmitri?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Not in my head, no.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: That's what I thought. Lena, do you have time to read it?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I can look at it this afternoon, yes. Do I send it to you?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Send it to the thread. Everyone sees.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Diego, can you get me the credit list from finance, per account, not just the total? Just so we know whose it is.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yeah. I'll email Sione, he usually does that for them.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Good. And Arjun, the sheet, the weekly numbers, split by postcode if you can.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Okay. Tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Dmitri, ring the account person. Don't promise anything.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I won't promise anything. I'll just ask.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So here's where I am. I hear the objection, and it's a real one. But I'm not going to change anything off one conversation, with the figures half in. Parcelwise stays as it is for now, and we come back to this next week with the split and the clause in hand.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: So we just wait.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: We gather what we need first. That's not nothing.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Fine. It's a week.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Can we make it the Thursday? Because I'm out Friday.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Thursday works. I'll move it.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Thursday's fine for me.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Oh, wait, before you go - the new rota for the weekend cover, is that still happening or did that get dropped?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Dropped, I think. Chidi said something. I'll check.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I've got to jump. Thanks, all.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Right, can we start with the racking inspection? Bao said it was booked but I never saw the date.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Twenty-third.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Morning or afternoon?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Morning. Eight.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is that the whole warehouse or just bay C? Because last time they only did-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Whole thing, I think. Two days, Bao said.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay, so I should tell the pickers to-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Wait for the notice. Dalia is writing it up.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Right, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Did the returns desk thing on the twenty-ninth go all right, by the way? I walked past and it looked-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It went fine. Diego, we've got parcels today.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Parcels, yes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Last week I said we'd come back with the postcode split and the contract clause. Arjun, numbers first.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Sheet's in the thread. Seventy-nine percent on time this week. Coastal is the worst, low seventies.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Seventy-nine? So that's, um, down from last time.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Two points down.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Hm. That's not really the direction I was expecting.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And the late count?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Round eight hundred since we started.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: The credits are up too. Sione sent me the list by account, it's about twenty-six hundred now. Two of the big accounts are most of it.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Two of the three who complained.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yeah, those.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I read the service part, finally. Page four, like Arjun said. They only owe us a credit if the monthly figure drops under seventy-five, and we're not under that overall, so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: So nothing.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Basically nothing. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Dmitri, did you get hold of the account person?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I did, yes. Spoke Tuesday. They said they're, uh, looking at the coastal depot. Staffing, I think.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Did they give you a date?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Not a date, no. Sort of a general, you know, they're aware of it.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So aware, no date.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: That's fair, yes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. I said last week I wouldn't move off one conversation with half the figures in. We've got the figures now, and they're worse. So I'm opening this up again, all of it, as if we hadn't picked anything.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Good. Because I've been wanting to say this for a week.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Go on then. And I'll argue the other side, someone should.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Lena and I went through the options last night. She did the comparison, honestly, so I'm mostly repeating her. Can I?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I can say it myself, I was-

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: You were on mute, I was there.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I wasn't, but fine, go on.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: So the two regionals, Eastline and Southgate. Average is four thirty-five a parcel, which is a bit more than Parcelwise, sure. But they put ninety-five percent on time in writing, and if they miss it we get credits back.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: And against what we were paying before the switch, it comes out about nine thousand a quarter ahead. Not thirteen and a half, but nine.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: The other thing is volume. Neither of them has a minimum. Parcelwise wants fifteen thousand parcels, and some quarters we're not far above that, so it's a bit of a trap.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Devil's advocate. Nine against thirteen is a worse headline. Why would I sign up for a worse headline?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Because thirteen wasn't real.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Arjun.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: The thirteen is before credits. Add twenty-six hundred and it's not thirteen.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Well, the credits could be a one-off-

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Seventy-nine, Dmitri.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And it's two couriers, so if Eastline has a bad week, then Southgate-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Not necessarily. They split by zone. Different postcodes, different ones.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: That's what I mean, it doesn't all fall over at once.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Fair. I raised the concentration thing myself in September.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: You did. Which reminds me of this driver I once had at my last place, he'd do the whole southern run alone, and when he took a week off the entire-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Diego.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Right. Not relevant. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: What worries me is the local coverage. Do the two of them actually cover every postcode we ship to?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Together, yes. I checked the zone maps. There's a couple of overlap postcodes near the border.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It's in the sheet. I don't remember them off the top.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Fine. And the Tuesday courier, is it one of these two?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: No, no. That one's gone. Neither of them does that.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: What about the exit from Parcelwise? Alejandra's email said what, three months' notice?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Um, I think it was three. I'd have to look.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It's three. Plus they can bill us till the end of the notice period.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So we'd be paying them for a bit even as we move.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I can live with that, if the alternative is another quarter at seventy-nine. Anyone against?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Not against. I mean, I did push for Parcelwise, so, but I'd rather the numbers were different.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Nobody's pinning it on you, Dmitri.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: No, thanks. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Fine by me.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Yes. From me too.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Then the south-east moves to Eastline and Southgate, split by postcode zone, and we give Parcelwise their notice.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Okay. I'll do the, uh, the Parcelwise letter, if someone gives me the clause number.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I'll put it in the thread, it's on page four.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Of course it is.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Lena, can you send me the zone map too? I'd like to see those overlap postcodes before anything goes out.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Yes, today.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Can I ask one unrelated thing? The weekend cover rota, did Chidi ever say?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: He said it's dropped. I forgot to tell you. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Oh. Okay. Good, I'd already said no to a wedding.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And the audit, Lena, is that the twenty-first or the twenty-second?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Twenty-second. I checked.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Good. I've got to run, I'm late for something. Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Bye.
